absent: Buddy coalescing and migratetype grouping inside buddy return and frozen page handling beyond flag forwarding.
Lock ordering between zone, barn and local sheaf guards and caller interrupt state expectations.
Numeric values and sizing formulas for watermarks, batch scales, sheaf capacities and retry limits.
Allocation slow paths, reclaim wakeup and compaction actions that consume watermark results.
Slab extension content, profiling, memory accounting and sanitizer hook implementations.
Deferred free queue mechanics and timing after lockless deferral.
Full struct definitions and lifetime rules for page, zone, slab, cache, sheaf and barn.
Trace event payloads and stability guarantees.

findings.text: Public release for general kernel objects that accepts null and zero tagged pointers as no-ops, traces the caller, resolves backing page and slab, sends large buddy allocations to dedicated teardown and slab objects to cache derived release.

Lock free release for sensitive contexts that accepts null, warns and drops large allocations as unsupported, runs only accounting and sanitizer hooks safe without spinning, then tries per CPU sheaf insertion and otherwise queues for deferred release.
Public watermark probe for a zone and order that supplies the current free page tally to the extended evaluator along with mark, zone ceiling and allocation flags.

Extended watermark evaluator that deducts unusable free pages, relaxes the minimum for reserve and victim classes, fails fast on order zero shortfall, and for higher orders requires a populated free list in a usable migratetype.
Reset for per node reclaim failure counter that atomically exchanges to zero and emits a trace only when the prior value was nonzero, keyed by node and reason.
Hopelessness test that reports true once the per node atomic failure counter reaches the configured maximum retry threshold.
Unlocked buddy return for frozen pages that forwards page and order to the shared frozen free path with the no lock indicator.
Leak detector release hook that ignores null and error tagged pointers unless free tracking is enabled, then removes the full object record for the address.
Fast path free into current CPU sheaf that requires the per cache local guard, replaces a full main sheaf when needed, appends the object, releases the guard and records a fast path event.

Bulk grouping helper that starts from one object, derives slab and cache when absent including large allocation bypass, links same slab objects with bounded lookahead, and compacts the input array by swapping matches forward.
Statistics accumulator that adds a delta to a per CPU cache counter for the given item when statistics are compiled in, otherwise no effect.

Per CPU drain walks requested page count to zero in round robin order over per CPU lists starting after the given index, skipping empty lists, converting each chosen index to an order, then repeatedly unlinking the tail page, adjusting both global and per CPU counts by pages per block, returning each block to the buddy with its block migratetype and tracing the event.

List index to order mapping divides by the count of per CPU migratetypes, and when transparent huge pages are enabled forces indexes beyond the low order range to the huge page middle directory order.

Drain batch selector returns the smaller of cached count and scaled batch when freeing high order, forces single page when high is below batch for disabled or boot sets, otherwise clamps the observed consecutive free count between batch and high minus batch.

High watermark tuner clamps stored high between observed minima and maxima, returns zero when disabled, lowers high on high order drain, caps caching during active reclaim, and otherwise shrinks on below high pressure or grows to accommodate batch plus recent frees.
Unusable free estimator starts from fragmentation allowance for the order, adds reserved high atomic pages unless reserve access is granted, and adds free CMA pages when the caller cannot use CMA.
Emptiness test for one order and migratetype that reports true when the corresponding free list has no entries.

Slab accounting reversal unconditionally releases object extension storage to cover profiling disable races, then subtracts the byte size of the compound slab from the node resident statistic chosen by cache kind.

Object extension teardown clears the handle when absent or marked failed, drops the reference when extensions live inside the slab without freeing, and for external storage frees via normal or lockless release according to spin permission before clearing.

Large allocation teardown derives order from compound metadata, warns on missing large marker or zero order, runs leak and sanitizer hooks, subtracts bytes from unreclaimable slab accounting, clears the large marker and returns pages to the buddy.

Empty sheaf allocator refuses recursion when flagged, masks object cgroup clearing bits from allocation flags, marks kmalloc caches non recursive to avoid deep stacks, allocates zeroed storage sized for capacity, links back to the cache and counts the event.

Main sheaf flush removes a bounded batch from the tail under the local guard, copies pointers aside, releases the guard before bulk freeing to avoid holding it across slab locks, counts flushed objects and repeats until empty; unused sheaf flush frees the whole content at once.
Bulk free driver skips empty calls, repeatedly builds same slab groups, bypasses fenced objects, and hands each group to slab release with caller address, continuing until all inputs are consumed.

Sheaf support test requires tiny builds disabled and nonzero capacity; barn lookup selects the current node entry of the cache; kmalloc flag helper routes through allocation hooks; lock assertion combines lockdep held check with probe attachment.
Single bit clear helper removes the pfmemalloc marker from slab flags.

Page allocator state observed here comprises zone with spin lock, free areas, low memory reserves, flags and high atomic reserve; free area with per order free count and per migratetype lists; per CPU pages with cached count, batch, consecutive free count, high tunables and indexed lists.

Slab state observed here comprises slab with flag word, cache back pointer and extension handle; cache with object size, flags, sheaf capacity, per CPU sheaves, per node barn pointers and per CPU statistics; node data with failure counter and identifier.

Sheaf caching state comprises per CPU record with main and spare sheaves; sheaf with owning cache, used size and object array plus barn linkage; node barn with spin lock, empty and full list heads and their counts.
Detached bulk group carries owning cache, target slab, head and tail link and object count for one same slab run.
Per CPU bulk drain holds the zone spin lock with interrupts saved across the whole unlink and buddy return loop via scoped guard.
Node barn list mutations run under the barn spin lock with interrupts saved; callers that forbid spinning use try acquisition and abort on contention while normal callers block.

Per cache per CPU sheaf access requires the local guard acquired by try lock; it is held while inspecting or swapping main and spare, released before sleeping allocation or bulk free, and reacquired before install, with lockdep assertion on held paths.

Full main replacement backs off for bootstrap or debug caches without sheaves and for missing node barn, reuses spare when absent or partially filled, otherwise swaps a full sheaf for an empty one at the barn, flushes spare when the barn is saturated, allocates a fresh empty when allowed, and on allocation failure flushes main and retries.

Empty sheaf install assumes no spare as the fast path, returns the fresh sheaf to the barn when main or spare gained space during the gap, and otherwise publishes the full main to the barn before installing the fresh empty as main.

Lockless free omits leak recursion, lock debugging, access checking and fencing helpers because they may spin, and documents that invalid free reporting from non maskable context may self deadlock as an acceptable cost of reporting a double bug.
Bulk drain clamps the requested count to the cached count to avoid spinning on empty lists and unlinks each page from its per CPU list before buddy return to avoid list corruption.

Large teardown warns once on missing large marker and on zero order; barn fast paths read empty and full counts outside the lock as racy hints and revalidate under the lock, returning distinct resource exhaustion versus contention signals.
Allocation flag names control watermark relaxation and list visibility for reserves, minimum reserve, non blocking, out of memory victim, CMA use and high atomic use.
Migratetype and per CPU geometry names define per CPU type count, list counts, low order boundary, huge page order and CMA and high atomic types used for index conversion and watermark scanning.

Tuning and accounting names observed are zone reclaim active and below high flags, batch scale maximum, node failure retry maximum, slab pfmemalloc bit, kmalloc cache bit, no recurse and default sheaf allocation modes, per CPU batch maximum, maximum retained full sheaves, frozen free modes, and free page and slab byte statistics.
